questions: If there are multiple simple paths from 1 to N with the same minimum XOR value, is it acceptable to output any of those values, or must we output the unique minimum value (which is the same for all)?
Are self-loops or multiple edges between the same pair of vertices allowed, given the graph is described as simple?
Should the XOR be computed over the sequence of edge labels in the order they are traversed, or is XOR commutative/associative making order irrelevant?
If no simple path exists from 1 to N (contradicting connectivity), how should we handle it?
Are the edge labels w_i integers, and should XOR be performed on their binary representations as non-negative integers up to 2^60?
Is the path required to be simple (no repeated vertices), and if a path repeats a vertex but not an edge, is it allowed?
Should the XOR include the label of the first edge traversed from vertex 1, or does it start from zero?
If the path consists of a single edge directly from 1 to N, is the XOR just w_i of that edge, or is there an implicit initial value?
